decisive_spans.text: She was not a smoker and did not have diabetes
Her body mass index was 19.22 kg/m²
The patient had untreated dyslipidemia (LDL cholesterol 3.11 mmol/L)
high-grade ostial stenosis of the left renal, celiac trunk, and superior mesenteric arteries

response.rationale: The patient's risk factors and imaging findings strongly support Atherosclerotic disease. The absence of smoking and diabetes, and a low BMI, contradict this diagnosis, but the presence of dyslipidemia and the specific pattern of ostial stenoses are highly suggestive. Fibromuscular dysplasia is a runner-up due to the renal artery stenosis and murmur, but the ostial nature of the stenoses and involvement of multiple visceral arteries make atherosclerosis more likely.
